title: hollow-can-only-see-the-files-the-chart-declared
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; cairn/devices/tester owns hollow
intention: cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py:428 takes its subject set from writes_to(ticket) — the decompose berth's hand-authored list of what the build will write. So the hollow reading measures WHAT THE CHART PREDICTED, not what the build DID. A file the build genuinely changed and the chart never named is not reverted, not run against, and not reported — it is silently outside the reading, and the run still prints a clean green. Make the subject set the UNION of writes_to and the files actually changed since the pre-build commit hollow already resolves, so an undeclared build file is measured (or, at minimum, NAMED as unmeasured) rather than invisible.
why: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, and hollow is the instrument that says so. An instrument whose field of view is drawn by the same hand it is auditing cannot see the thing that hand forgot. Law 7 — the run prints '2 file(s) measured · 0 hollow' with no line anywhere saying a third file was changed and skipped, which collapses 'measured clean' into 'not looked at'. And Law 3 — 'this build is not hollow' is a claim about the build, and today it is only a claim about the declaration.
how: hollow.measure() already resolves the pre-build commit (the BUILDME crossing's HEAD) and already builds a worktree at the current HEAD. `git diff --name-only <pre-build>..HEAD` in that same worktree is therefore free and is the honest subject set. Two candidate shapes, and the choice is the build's: (1) measure the union — every changed file gets reverted and run like any other, which makes the reading complete but can only widen it; or (2) keep measuring writes_to and REPORT the difference — 'changed but not declared: <files>' as a loud line and a field on the seal. Prefer (1) with (2)'s line kept, because a named-but-unmeasured file is still a hole a caller can walk past. _classify()'s existing skips (instruments, records, outside-repo) apply unchanged to the widened set.
falsifier: DONE when a fixture ticket whose build changes a file its decompose berth does not name produces a hollow run that either REDS that file or NAMES it as changed-and-unmeasured — and a control run, where the berth names everything the build touched, reads identically to today. WRONG INTENT if the widening is satisfied by trusting writes_to harder (a sieve that reds an incomplete berth at chart time is a different, useful ticket and does not close this one): the point is that hollow stops depending on a declaration being complete, not that declarations get scolded.
traces_to: Law 8 (the hollow reading IS the proof-that-a-hollow-build-couldn't-pass; a reading with a hand-drawn field of view is not one); Law 7 (a diagnostic surface may not print a green over a file it never looked at); Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — and today what is measured is the chart, not the build).
watchme: none, because the fix's own control pair is the standing check: the fixture ticket with an incomplete berth must red and the complete one must not, and both live in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/. A probe counting undeclared-file events in the wild would measure how often charts are incomplete — a real question, and a DIFFERENT one from whether the instrument can see them.
gates_bound: proof gate — cairn/devices/tester/proofs/ runs green under the tester at isolation=netns, and the new tooth reds against today's writes_to-only subject set.
feeds back to origin on failure — a red routes to this ticket's own voyage, never to a paragraph.
durability gate — not done until proven AND committed.
children: none, because it is one subject-set resolution inside one function

measured_at_cast.reading: `cairn test --hollow 548dd13fb4db --seal` reported '2 file(s) measured · 1 skipped' — host.py and probes/an_agent_retry_gets_a_fresh_sample.py. The same voyage ALSO changed cairn/devices/inference_domain/device.py (commit 1b2f223, the _handle_resolve whitelist that had been dropping the `tools` key), and device.py appears nowhere in the run. Its revert would red test_a_toolset_survives_the_bus_verb BY NAME, so the file is not merely unmeasured — it is the one file in the voyage whose coverage was in question.
measured_at_cast.cause: hollow.py:428 `files = writes_to(ticket, berths_root=berths_root)`; the decompose berth for 548dd13fb4db predates the discovery of the bus-verb defect and names host.py and the probe only.
measured_at_cast.not_a_defect_of_this_voyage: The berth was honest when it was written — the defect was found after charting. That is exactly the case the fix must cover, because it is the normal case: a voyage that finds nothing new needs no widening.

decisions.text: Shape (1) with (2)'s line, as the ticket's how prefers: the subject set is the UNION of writes_to(ticket) and the files git says changed between the pre-build commit and HEAD; every file in the union is classified and measured exactly as a declared one is today, AND the finding gains a field undeclared: [<repo-relative files in the diff but not in writes_to>] that the CLI prints as one loud line 'changed but not declared: a, b' (or nothing when empty). No trust in writes_to is added and no chart-time sieve is built (WRONG INTENT clause).
decisions.step: unlisted: decide implementation approach — measure union of declares+actual, or report-only

decisions.text: One edit in hollow.measure at hollow.py:445, after commit = prebuild_commit(...): changed = git -C <repo_root> diff --name-only <commit>..HEAD (run with git_env(), non-zero exit -> HollowUnmeasurable naming the command, as prebuild_commit already does); declared = writes_to(...) normalised through _inside; files = declared + [c for c in changed if c not in declared] in that order; undeclared = the appended tail. Live repo, not the worktree — the diff is between two commits and the worktree is at HEAD anyway.
decisions.step: unlisted: modify hollow.measure() to obtain actual changed files via git diff

decisions.text: _classify (hollow.py:306) is not touched: it already runs per file in the measurement loop (hollow.py:~577 for rel in files: why = _classify(rel)), so instruments, records and outside-repo files in the widened set are skipped with the same named reasons and land in skipped like today; an undeclared file that is skipped is still listed under undeclared (the two facts are separate, Law 7).
decisions.step: unlisted: apply _classify() skips unchanged to the widened file set

decisions.text: No new fixture world: test_hollow.py's _fixture (proofs/test_hollow.py:108) already commits two files that change in the build (subject.py, unchecked.py) and _berth_decompose(tmp, files) already takes the declared list. The proof for this ticket is a new file cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow_sees_undeclared_files.py importing those helpers, with two teeth: (1) incomplete berth — _berth_decompose(tmp, ['subject.py', 'proofs/test_fixture.py']) then measure(...) — asserts f['undeclared'] == ['unchecked.py'], 'unchecked.py' in f['measured'] and in f['hollow'] (the file reds no tooth), verdict 'red'; (2) control — the berth names subject.py, unchecked.py, proofs/test_fixture.py — asserts f['undeclared'] == [] and every other finding key equals the reading test_hollow's first tooth pins today. PROVES = {'39966e1cefe4': {'1': tooth 1, '2': tooth 2}}; both run under the tester, netns, twice, before PROVEME.
decisions.step: unlisted: create fixture tickets with incomplete and complete decompose berths

decisions.text: The CLI's hollow report (cli.py, the --hollow arm that prints 'N file(s) measured · M hollow') prints one extra line only when f['undeclared'] is non-empty: '  changed but not declared: ' + ', '.join(undeclared). The seal's evidence.hollow carries the whole finding already, so the field rides the seal with no further edit; test_hollow's tooth 'evidence_hollow_lands_inside_the_seal_and_the_eight_fields_still_stand' is updated to nine fields (undeclared added) — that tooth's edit is the one existing-proof change, named here so it is not a surprise at reseal.
